parsed.same_study_reason: Both lists critique the same analysis of the returns to science weighed against biotech and extinction risks. Both refer to XPT forecasts, superforecasters versus domain experts, the discount rate (epistemic regime), and the time of perils.

pairs.reason: Both say the preference for superforecaster over domain-expert estimates is too strong or not robustly justified, which leaves the conclusions fragile. A2 also covers the discount-rate justification, so it is broader.

Both target the regime-based discount rate and note that results are sensitive to it. A2 objects to its inconsistent justification: it extrapolates a 20-year AI forecast. B9 objects that it lumps several hazards into one constant p and assumes policy does not affect it.
Both raise discounting inconsistency. A2 is about how the 2% rate is justified; B2 is about inconsistent discounting, population and income across regimes in the λW term.
Both involve turning XPT forecasts into model parameters. A2 concerns the discount rates implied by that extrapolation; B7 concerns hazard-mapping transformations whose uncertainty is not propagated.

Both note that AI may dominate capabilities and risk. A1 objects that AI risk is left out of the risk comparison; B1 objects that marginal changes in the pace of science may not shift the modeled hazards at all.
Both concern weighing the benefits of science against biotech risk. A1 faults the omission of AI risk; B12 faults weakly identified attribution of historical benefits.
